Comments: On June 11, 2026, the Department conducted a Follow Up Inspection of Oil and Gas Mgmt's Armstrong 2 gas well site direct access road following IR 4203618, where violations were continued for an inadequately stabilized shared and direct access road.A NOV response has yet to be received from the operator of this gas well following IR 3891447 when violations were issued for an inadequately stabilized shared and direct access road. However, the DEP has been in communication with the other operator who utilizes the shared portion of the access road. At the time of this inspection, the Department observed the shared access road to be permanent stabilized with gravel. Silt-fencing was observed to be installed on the side of the access road closest to the stream, and culverts and berms appear to be installed to direct water off of/away from the access road.At the time of this inspection, it appears that conditions of the direct portion of the access road leading to the Armstrong 2 gas well site are unchanged from IR 3891447, rutting and large pooling of stormwater were observed throughout the access road and an area of erosion as exposed a line from underground. No fluid leaks or fluid discharges were observed to be coming from the exposed surface of this line at the time of this inspection. Although the Department observed the shared portion of the access road to be stabilized, site observations of the direct portion of the access road are unchanged. Therefore, based on today's inspection, violations issued for an inadequately stabilized direct access road are to remain outstanding at this time.Violations associated with the Department's observations of the gas well site are assessed in IR 4203643.

Inspection Date: 7/31/2023
Comments: Onsite to investigate Complaint # 373782 dated 7/20/2023 and a follow-up inspection to Inspection Report # 3589928 dated 7/21/2023. An onsite meeting was scheduled with Petro Erie Inc. and the Department which developed this Inspection Report.Individuals present at the onsite meeting:Harry Rhoades -Owner/Operator of Petro Erie Inc.Chris Rhoades -Driver for Harry RhoadesRob Bechtel -PA DEPRick Willey -PA DEPAlan Wolf -PA DEPLucas Eichner -PA DEPSteve Wells -PA DEPThe meeting was started off by Rob Bechtel stating the reason for the meeting and what was discovered during a previous site inspection on 7/21/2023 with violations cited. It was discussed that there is a potential that the discharge of produced fluid from the tank battery may have impacted the Reno, PA public water supply. Mr. Rhoades asked if the pubic water supply was now safe to drink and if regular testing was being conducted. We informed him that the oil and gas program was collecting samples for analysis to determine if the water supply was impacted by oil and gas activity and that the Safe Drinking Water program was working with Venango Water Company related to the public water supply. properties.content:
Report Details
Operator: Eqt Prod Co
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 2019-03-14
Violation Code: SWMA 301 - MANAGEMENT OF RESIDUAL WASTE - Person operated a residual waste processing or disposal facility without obtaining a permit for such facility from DEP. Person stored, transported, processed, or disposed of residual waste inconsistent with or unauthorized by the rules and regulations of DEP.
Violation ID: 844717
Permit API: 059-26084
Unconventional: Yes
County: Greene
Municipality: Center Twp
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 2019-03-14
Comments: On Tuesday March 12, 2019 I received notification of a produced water release, which was discovered and reported to the Department the preceding evening, at the Pierce Well Site located in Center Township, Greene County. On Tuesday, while on-site to assess the situation, I spoke on the telephone with Ms. Carey Valor Bell from EQT Production Company (EQT) regarding details of the incident and the remediation. I also conducted site visits on Wednesday March 13 and two (2) site visits on Thursday March 14 to check on the progress of remediation activities. Ms. Valor Bell was also present during the March 14 afternoon site visit. What was assumed to be an estimated two (2) to three (3) gallons of produced fluid was discovered at the Pierce Well Pad on March 11. The fluid was observed to be "bubbling up" through the well pad gravel along the northeastern side of the well pad behind the GPUs. Upon discovery, the GPU was shut-in to prevent any additional,flow through the dump line which runs between the GPU and the production fluid ASTs. Following further investigation, it was discovered that the initial estimated quantity was low given that the released fluid appeared to be seeping out of the slope immediately below and adjacent to the dump line. EQT currently estimates approximately 30 gallons of produced fluid had leaked from the dump line. A different remediation contractor was mobilized to the site to continue with the investigation and remediation. During the initial excavation of the well pad gravel, water was observed entering the excavation from the pad gravels which was assumed to be precipitation. Given that water was entering the excavation and the forecast for additional precipitation, a sump was installed in the excavation on the pad to dewater the area into a flow-back tank. The collected water will be monitored until conductivity readings meet applicable standards, at which time the well pad will be further investigated and remediated. While dewatering of the initial excavation continued, soil conductivity probes were used to delineate the extent of impact on the well pad slope below the GPU. The excavation limit was approximately in line with the outside edge of the GPU associated with well 591982 (059-26084) and extended approximately 10 to 12 feet west. The excavation was deepest (approximately 18 inches) along the eastern end of the excavation and was estimated to be approximately six (6) inches in depth along the western end of the excavation. A soil conductivity probe was also used to confirm that all impacted materials had been removed. Additional material was removed to assure remediation was complete. Conductivity readings collected following excavation activities were all less than or equal to 1 mS/cm. The impacted material was containerized and sampled for off-site disposal. The excavated area was stabilized with seed and mulch. Silt fence was also set up along the downslope side of the excavation. The sump was still running and connected to the flow-back tank as observed on a March 20, 2019 site visit. The release of produced fluid from the dump line and impact to native materials is a violation of 35 P.S. Section 6018.301 and 25 Pa. Code, Sections 78a.54 and 78a.57(a). The operator should respond according to the instructions provided in this notice.

Violation ID: 907830
Permit API: 081-21846
Unconventional: Yes
County: Lycoming
Municipality: Cascade Twp
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 2/10/2021
Comments: This inspection was conducted in response to a notification from the operator that drilling mud sprayed from a flare stack during a gas kick which impacted the pad surface and an adjacent area within the LOD on February 6, 2021. The site was snow-covered during this inspection. DEP EP Specialist Justin Abbott accompanied me on this inspection. We met with company man Bill Mitchell upon arriving on location. The rig is finishing the 2nd of 5 wells on the pad. The release occurred while the cementing the A-1H well. According to the company man on location, the drilling mud sprayed northeast of the flare stack. The mud spray landed on containment, in the travel lane along the northeast edge of the pad, and in the area within the LOD along the northeast side of the pad. Impacted snow was removed by skid steer and with shovels. The impacted snow was placed in a container for disposal. The mud residue could be observed on the well site secondary containment, on a battery of frac tanks, on several chemical totes, and on a light cover. No residue was observed on the pad surface or anywhere off of the pad. New snowfall the day before this inspection made an examination of the pad surface and the soil off of the pad difficult. According to an email sent on February 11, 2021 to the Department, Rick Hall of ARD stated that most of what impacted the snow off of the secondary containment was ash from drilling mud that was combusted by the flare stack. He stated that based on a minimal amount of fluid off containment, the small area impacted, and interviews with the company man and cleanup personnel, that the estimated release volume is less than 5 gallons. The Department requests a notification when the drilling rig is removed from the pad. Violations noted and considered immediately corrected.

Violation ID: 993539
Permit API: 083-48749
Unconventional: No
County: McKean
Municipality: Lafayette Twp
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 5/01/2023
Comments: This inspection was conducted in response to the notification by Cliff Easton of Consortium Energy of a crude oil release from a buried gathering line located approximately 150 feet to the south of this conventional well.Upon my arrival onsite, Cliff and I evaluated the section of roadside ditch where oil was discovered, which is within approximately ten feet of an unnamed tributary (UNT) of Turnup Run. The gathering lines for the Warrant 3410 lease are located within this ditch, therefore a failure of one of these lines is the likely culprit. Consortium has shut in all of the wells on the lease and has placed absorbent pads and peat across the ditch floor to prevent any appreciable oil from reaching the stream. At this time, only a slight emulsion is present in the UNT of Turnup Run, no sheen or free product was observed upon agitating the stream. It appears that the released crude oil remains in the soil within the ditch. Booms and pads have been placed at the inlet and near the outlet of a culvert that carries the stream across the lease road as a precaution. Consortium was coordinating with local contractors to begin excavating the contaminated soil and confirm/repair the source of the release. I advised Cliff to maintain the containment in the ditch and to regularly check the booms in the UNT of Turnup Run. If any appreciable amount of oil is discovered in the stream, please contact the Department. Cliff stated that production would not continue on the lease until the lines in this ditch are repaired or replaced.Upcoming inspections will be conducted to evaluate remediation efforts and if there is any additional impact to the UNT of Turnup Run.

Comments: This inspection was conducted in response to a report of a release discovered by the operator on August 22, 2020. DEP EP specialist Justin Abbott accompanied me on this inspection and we were met by Mike Deming of SWN on site. According to Mr. Deming, fluid was found between the layers of the secondary containment near where the blender had been during the recent frac. He said that the containment was removed in this area and puddles of fluid with elevated conductivity (EC) were discovered on the pad surface. He said that a spill of 10 gallons of produced water had been spilled on the secondary containment during the frac in this area and he believed that this release was related. At the time of this inspection, the area impacted by the release had already been excavated. The EC readings in this area on the Hanna soil conductivity meter were all less than 1 mS/cm. Mr. Deming said that approximately 60 tons of material had been excavated in an area approximately 60 ft x 80 ft. He estimated the spill volume at 10 gallons based on this information. Some puddles with EC ranging between 2 to 3 mS/cm were observed on the pad. The puddles were located in travel lanes on the pad. Mr. Deming said that he believed that these were due to the truck traffic bringing magnesium chloride onto the pad because magnesium chloride is used for dust control on the access road. The Department recommends sucking up these puddles as needed.Violations noted and considered immediately corrected.

Person stored, transported, processed, or disposed of residual waste inconsistent with or unauthorized by the rules and regulations of DEP.
Violation ID: 8232156
Permit API: 125-28458
Unconventional: Yes

Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 5/01/2025
Comments: On May 1, 2025, an inspection was conducted in response to a spill at the Malinky well pad in Smith Township, Washington County. According to the incident report that was submitted by Range Resources representative Nate Smiell, approximately 200 gallons of diethylene glycol was released to the surface of the well pad on the day of this inspection at 11:27 AM. No waterways are reported to have been impacted and remediation crew is on the way for cleanup. This spill report was submitted to the Department on the day of this inspection at 12:45 PM. Mr. Smiell was present onsite for this inspection. Additional representatives from Range Resources and SPSI were also onsite conducting remediation.Upon arrival, the Department spoke with Mr. Smiell who further explained that diethylene glycol was being pumped from the GPU units in preparation for installation of secondary containment, per the requirements of an active Consent Order and Agreement (CO and A) between the operator and the Department, when the pump truck operator erroneously pumped the diethylene glycol from the GPU into a chamber of the truck tank that was already full. This resulted in an estimated 200 gallons of diethylene glycol being released from a vent on the top of the truck's vessel and to the surface of well pad. Three spill cleanup drums were filled with absorbent material that soaked up the standing ethylene glycol on the well pad surface. Two rolloff boxes are expected to be required to contain the impacted material. Mr. Smiell then confirmed that the operator will conduct remediation in accordance with the requirements of Act 2. Mr. Smiell reported that at the time of this inspection, the majority of the impacted material appears to have been removed. This is based on testing that was conducted by Mr. Smiell throughout the impacted area, utilizing a glycol test kit, however a third-party environmental consultant is scheduled to take confirmation samples on the day following this inspection, per the requirements of Act 2. Excavation and remediation of the impacted area remains ongoing at the time of inspection (see photos 4-8, 12, and 17-19). The following was observed:The Act 9 sign is installed at the entrance of the access road and is not obscured from view by vegetation, in accordance with 78a.55 (see photo 1). Some minor potholes were observed in the access road (see photo 2). The Emergency Response Plan (ERP) is onsite (see photo 3). No Safety Data Sheet (SDS) was located onsite for diethylene glycol, the pollutant released during this incident. The GPU units are in the process of being equipped with secondary containment (see photo 9). The production tanks and the surrounding secondary containment do not have any observable fluid leaks (see photo 10). Well 2H is equipped with a well tag with no staining or evidence of fluid leaks to the ground around it, and it appears to be in production (see photos 14 and 15). Six additional wells are onsite that appear to be in production (see photo 13).Based on observations from this inspection, violations shall be issued from this inspection for releasing pollutants to the surface of the ground and for failure to keep the SDS onsite for the pollutant released.

Comments: On August 12, 2025, the Department conducted an Incident Inspection of Range Resources Conner Samuel well site, located in Cecil Township, Washington County in response to a spill that was reported to the DEP hotline on 8/11/2025 at 8:44pm by Range. Accompanying on today's inspection is Range Resources representative Kevin Rudd.According to the report and Mr. Rudd, after finishing the cement job on the 4H, a flow line became over pressurized due to a valve being left closed. This resulted in a 10 cap dislodging from the flow line and releasing approximately 21 gallons of a synthetic oil based mud (SOBM) fine mist on to the graveled well pad and approximately 42 gallons on to the secondary containment. According to Range, prior to this inspection, the fine mist release was remediated in accordance with 78a66(c)(1) and disposal documents will be provided to the Department upon its receipt.At the time of this inspection, the Act 9 Sign was observed at the access road entrance with all required information posted on it, and in the on-site mailbox was the Emergency Response Plan and Preparedness, Prevention and Contingency Plan, both of which had all required components. The access road was observed to be stabilized with gravel and the well site perimeters were observed to be exhibiting at least 70% uniform and adequate vegetative growth with no erosion or sedimentation issues observed.At the time of this inspection, the Department observed the release area to be approximately 12ft x 20ft and comprised of had freshly laid gravel. No SOBM was observed on the gravel or on the secondary containment in this area at the time of this inspection. The Department utilized a conductivity meter to screen the gravel well pad in this release area, and collected soil conductivity readings of 0.0002 mS, in three different locations as well as 0.0651 mS, and 0.0028 mS. These soil conductivity readings are comparable to the background soil conductivity reading of 0.0213 mS, which was collected upslope and adjacent to the well site in a vegetated area.At the time of this inspection, the Department requested Safety Data Sheets (SDSs) for the SOBM involved in the release as well as secondary containment inspection logs. At the time of this inspection, Mr. Rudd provided the Department with the secondary containment logs and attempted to email the Department an electronic copy of the SDSs, however, that email was not received, therefore the Department is again requesting that SDSs for the SOBM be provided to the Department within 2 business days of the receipt of this inspection report.Based on observations made at the time of this inspection, it appears that Range remediated the release in accordance with 78a66(c)(1), therefore, violations are noted and immediately corrected.Transmittal of this inspection report is delayed due to an app IT error.

properties.content:
Report Details

Violation Code: 78a57(a) - CONTROL, STORAGE AND DISPOSAL OF PRODUCTION FLUIDS - Operator failed to collect brine and other fluids produced during operation of the well in a tank, series of tanks, or other device approved by the Department for subsequent disposal or reuse.
Violation ID: 880969
Permit API: 115-20843
Unconventional: Yes
County: Susquehanna
Municipality: Gibson Twp
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 2020-03-18
Comments: Brody Webster, contacted Gene Rickard by phone on March 17, 2020 at 4:27 PM to report that a spill had occurred on COG's Davis G Well Pad located in Gibson Township, Susquehanna County. The spill had occurred on March 14, 2020 at 10:00 AM while a service rig (Consolidated Wellsite Services) was on location to remove the 2 3/8-inch production tubing from the 2H well. During the operation, it was determined that there was debris (sand, shale fragments, etc.) within the production tubing causing fluid (primarily freshwater that had been introduced to the well) to be retained inside the pipe as it was brought to the surface. As each 30' segment of tubing was recovered and separated at the threaded connection, the fluid was drained from the pipe to the sealed well cellar (6' diameter metal cellar with cement base) and subsequently recovered by vacuum truck. During the process, a limited volume of the fluid sprayed/misted outside of the cellar and impacted an area of soil near the 2H well cellar. Approximately 7 to 8 cubic yards of visibly impacted soils were excavated and placed into a lined roll-off container for off-site disposal at an approved facility. Resource Environmental has been contracted to characterize the remaining soils. The reason the 2 3/8-inch pipes held water was because it was discovered that the pipe was plugged at the bottom by sand and other debris. Probably the reason for the pipes removal in the first place. The spill volume was reported as 22 gallons of produced and freshwater mixed together.

Unconventional: Yes

Comments: At time of inspection: On site for a post-plugging inspection of the Phoenix 590796 (117-20970) well to confirm the current condition of this previously leaking plugged well. Upon arrival I met with Penn Mechanical Group reps. Mike Nelson and Art Brocilous. The plugged well was open and vented (see photo #1). The cellar was empty with dirt on the bottom. The casing was full of water and there was no bubbling noticed. Mike checked the depth of the gravel (approximately 3') in the well with a fiberglass rod that was in the casing. The well started bubbling when the gravel was disturbed (see photo #2). The bubbling lasted about 15 to 20 seconds then quit. I asked Mike to disturb the gravel again so I could confirm that the bubbling wasn't from trapped gas in the well. There was no gas detected at the plugged well with a Remote Methane Leak Detector (RMLD-CS) or an Altair 5x gas meter. The previous bubbling noted in wellbore and cellar area appears to have dissipated or has been remediated. Since no updates of remedial work performed have been received from operator since last response of 9/9/2023. The Dept. requests operator respond with the dates and specifics of any remedial work that was performed on this well, and provide the results of any isotopic samples of the previously detected gas, if any were collected. Please respond to this request within 10 days of the receipt of this Insp. Please send response to: David Schoonover at davschoono@pa.gov

Comments: On March 11, 2026, the Department conducted a follow up inspection in response to IRs 4157087, 4157136, and 4157162. This inspection is separated into 2 inspection reports. The narrative of both inspection reports are identical except for references to photos. This is inspection 1 of 2. A COA with the Department was entered into on 3/07/2019. According to the COA, the Operator shall restore the site within 9 months of plugging. At this time, plugging operations have not yet commenced and there is currently no rig on-site. Earth disturbance for site preparation has commenced.This inspection is being conducted with Aquatic Biologist 2s Christy Owens (DEP) and Miles Hegedus (DEP) to identify possible streams and wetland along the access road.Culvert 1 crossing (Photos 1-2) appears to be culverted for a roadside ditch. The outlet appears to be blocked due to soil moved during access road clearing.Culvert 2 crossing (P 3-4) appears to be a stream crossing. The outlet to the culvert appears to be blocked.Culvert 3 crossing (P 5-7) appears to be a stream crossing. The inlet to the culvert appears to be blocked.Culvert 4 crossing (P 8-9) appears to be culverted for a roadside ditch, however this culvert is not receiving water at this time due to the operator disturbing the channel causing water to be diverted further down the access road (P 10-12). The source of the water appears to be due to a seep which is causing early stages of wetland formation. The disturbed channel appears to be carrying fine sediment (Photos 10-11) towards the stream at culvert 5, however no sediment was observed entering the stream due to the second half of the channel going subsurface with the entry point into the stream unseen.Culvert 5 crossing (P 13-15) appears to be a stream crossing. E and S off of the access road was observed during the previous inspection earlier today above the outlet at culvert 5, however no sediment is observed entering the stream at this time.Just past culvert 5 on the inlet side appears to be a wetland (P 16).Culvert 6 crossing (P 17-19) appears to be culverted for a roadside ditch. The inlet of the culvert appears to be partially blocked. E and S off of the access road was observed during the previous inspection earlier today above the outlet at culvert 6. The erosion and sedimentation at this area appears to stop near the end of the culvert.Culvert 7 crossing (P 20-21) appears to be culverted for a roadside ditch. The inlet appears to be partially blocked and the outlet cannot be seen at this time due to brush.Culvert 8 crossing (P 22-25) appears to be a stream crossing. CFS is observed to be installed and functioning properly above the inlet side of the culvert. Upstream from the inlet of the stream and near the soil stockpile in this area, the Department observed newly moved soil that has been pushed into the stream channel.The Department recommends the operator install CFS along the access road in all sections of E and S off of the access road and above each culvert inlet and outlet, as well as gravel the access road at all culvert crossings in accordance with the E and S plan.The Department recommends the operator install orange construction fence along the access road near the seep and wetland identified near the culvert 4 inlet and past culvert 5 (P 8, 10-12, 16).The Department recommends removing sediment from the stream channel at culvert 8.The Department recommends the operator restore the roadside ditch at seep.Violations were issued in IR 4157087 for accelerated E and S, for failing to construct the site in accordance with the E and S plan, and for failing to maintain access road culverts in an inspection that was conducted earlier today prior to this inspection with Department Biologists. Therefore these violations are not included in this inspection report.New violations are being issued for sediment discharge into a stream, impact to wetland, and failing to identify wetlands and streams on the E and S plans.

Municipality: Redstone Township
Inspection Type: Follow-up Inspection
Inspection Date: 3/11/2026
Comments: On March 11, 2026, the Department conducted a follow up inspection in response to IRs 4157087, 4157136, and 4157162. This inspection is separated into 2 inspection reports. The narrative of both inspection reports are identical except for references to photos. This is inspection 1 of 2. A COA with the Department was entered into on 3/07/2019. According to the COA, the Operator shall restore the site within 9 months of plugging. At this time, plugging operations have not yet commenced and there is currently no rig on-site. Earth disturbance for site preparation has commenced.This inspection is being conducted with Aquatic Biologist 2s Christy Owens (DEP) and Miles Hegedus (DEP) to identify possible streams and wetland along the access road.Culvert 1 crossing (Photos 1-2) appears to be culverted for a roadside ditch. The outlet appears to be blocked due to soil moved during access road clearing.Culvert 2 crossing (P 3-4) appears to be a stream crossing. The outlet to the culvert appears to be blocked.Culvert 3 crossing (P 5-7) appears to be a stream crossing. The inlet to the culvert appears to be blocked.Culvert 4 crossing (P 8-9) appears to be culverted for a roadside ditch, however this culvert is not receiving water at this time due to the operator disturbing the channel causing water to be diverted further down the access road (P 10-12). The source of the water appears to be due to a seep which is causing early stages of wetland formation. The disturbed channel appears to be carrying fine sediment (Photos 10-11) towards the stream at culvert 5, however no sediment was observed entering the stream due to the second half of the channel going subsurface with the entry point into the stream unseen.Culvert 5 crossing (P 13-15) appears to be a stream crossing. E and S off of the access road was observed during the previous inspection earlier today above the outlet at culvert 5, however no sediment is observed entering the stream at this time.Just past culvert 5 on the inlet side appears to be a wetland (P 16).Culvert 6 crossing (P 17-19) appears to be culverted for a roadside ditch. The inlet of the culvert appears to be partially blocked. E and S off of the access road was observed during the previous inspection earlier today above the outlet at culvert 6. The erosion and sedimentation at this area appears to stop near the end of the culvert.Culvert 7 crossing (P 20-21) appears to be culverted for a roadside ditch. The inlet appears to be partially blocked and the outlet cannot be seen at this time due to brush.Culvert 8 crossing (P 22-25) appears to be a stream crossing. CFS is observed to be installed and functioning properly above the inlet side of the culvert. Upstream from the inlet of the stream and near the soil stockpile in this area, the Department observed newly moved soil that has been pushed into the stream channel.The Department recommends the operator install CFS along the access road in all sections of E and S off of the access road and above each culvert inlet and outlet, as well as gravel the access road at all culvert crossings in accordance with the E and S plan.The Department recommends the operator install orange construction fence along the access road near the seep and wetland identified near the culvert 4 inlet and past culvert 5 (P 8, 10-12, 16).The Department recommends removing sediment from the stream channel at culvert 8.The Department recommends the operator restore the roadside ditch at seep.Violations were issued in IR 4157087 for accelerated E and S, for failing to construct the site in accordance with the E and S plan, and for failing to maintain access road culverts in an inspection that was conducted earlier today prior to this inspection with Department Biologists. Therefore these violations are not included in this inspection report.New violations are being issued for sediment discharge into a stream, impact to wetland, and failing to identify wetlands and streams on the E and S plans.

Comments: On site Monday (11/30/20) for the start up of Step Pressure Build Up Tests (SPBUTs). There are (5) wells on this pad, they are the Hunter 5H, 6H, 21HC, 22HC and the 23HC. All (5) wells were in production. The (9x5), (13x9) and the (20x13) annuli of all the wells are plumbed to surface w/ rubber lines, the (20x13) annuli are venting to atmosphere via Sentry valves. The (13x9) and (9x5) annuli are sharing a 2" vent line to the production tanks. All annuli have transponders installed and are being monitored by the Operator. The ball valves were closed on all (20x13) annuli vents before there common vent line in order to isolate each annuli individually for gas checks being performed today for the beginning of the (SPBUTs).- Operator rep. (Tom Vitella) was on site to shut in the (20x13) annuli. - An ALTAIR 5X gas meter (cal.11/12/20) was turned on and gas checks performed @ the (20x13) Sentry valves showed no gas at time of shut in. - The (20x13) annuli were shut in @ 10:00, marking the start of the (SPBUTs). End of testing will be on Thurs. (12/3/20).
